summary: Georgia returns from its bye to face Florida in Atlanta. Ball security and secondary availability remain central after the Auburn loss. The following trip to Ole Miss now has a 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff.

items.headline: Georgia–Florida moves to Atlanta for Saturday’s game
items.tldr: The teams meet at Mercedes-Benz Stadium at 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC. Plan for Atlanta’s venue and travel details rather than the usual Jacksonville trip.

items.headline: Bolden’s availability remains a question after Auburn
items.tldr: DawgNation’s bye-week report described his absence and Georgia’s safety depth. Watch the next availability report; the earlier update did not establish a return date.

items.headline: Smart identifies Stockton’s injury as a shoulder stinger
items.tldr: The bye-week explanation distinguished the injury from a concussion. Keep that diagnosis separate from a guarantee about contact or workload in the next game.

items.headline: The late Auburn loss puts ball security in focus
items.tldr: Georgia lost 27-24 on October 17 after a late turnover gave Auburn another chance. Carry the possession lesson forward without treating a bye week as proof it is fixed.

items.headline: Georgia–Ole Miss is set for 7:30 p.m. ET on ABC
items.tldr: The November 7 trip follows this week’s Florida game. The new television window gives fans an evening Eastern start to plan around.

lead.headline: Finish the possession you have.
lead.body: Secure the football through pressure and contact before looking for extra yards. On defense, communicate the safety assignment early and make the next quarterback throw through a complete coverage.

matchup.thesis: Make ball security part of the play
matchup.question: What should fans watch in the next game?
matchup.answer: Give the quarterback a usable outlet and a clear decision about when the down is over. Keep the back end aligned so defensive pressure does not create an uncovered escape throw.

signals.title: Possession security
signals.summary: Know when to end the down
signals.detail: Watch the ball through the exchange, pocket movement and first contact. Take the available gain before an extra step puts the possession at risk.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with possession security?

signals.title: Quarterback protection
signals.detail: Give the quarterback an immediate receiving answer when the pocket narrows. Judge the plan by the decision it permits rather than the contact he can absorb.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with quarterback protection?

signals.title: Safety communication
signals.detail: Confirm the available personnel, then watch how the safeties exchange routes and run support. Keep a substitute’s assignment clear before the ball is snapped.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with safety communication?

signals.title: Run fits and safety support
signals.detail: Hold the edge while the inside defender closes the cutback. Keep the fit connected to safety support before committing to the first ball fake.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with run fits and safety support?
